quote: I get a lot of ladies, but who has time to keep track of all those feelings and memories and shit? I use Cairn to track my ladies and impress them with how well I pay attention.
It’s kinda like a high school locker room, but with search.
She said I never remember anything she tells me. Joke’s on her: I remember everything. I just have to search for it first.
Third date, I brought up her childhood rabbit by name. She called it “unsettling.” I call it retrieval-augmented romance.
I have a folder called “Women who said they liked my laugh.” It’s one note. It’s my mom.
My AI drafts my anniversary texts from 47 observations about my wife. She cried. Pretty sure it was the good kind.
I tagged every first date #lead. My therapist says that’s “a lot.”
Before Cairn I had to remember which girl hated cilantro. Now the cilantro remembers for me.
I wrote a relation: [[Me]] → deserves → [[Better]]. The graph doesn’t lie.
My ex asked if I kept anything of hers. Technically? A vault.
My wingman is a markdown file and honestly he’s more supportive than Derek.
I asked my AI what my love language is. It said “bullet points.”
I keep a running note of every compliment I’ve ever received. It’s mostly from waiters but it’s growing.
She asked what I’m passionate about, so I read her my top tags out loud. Tag cloud, baby.
Rule one of dating: never forget her dog’s name. Rule two: never let her find the note about her dog’s name.
I tried to get my AI to forget my ex. It said the prior revision is kept. Even the software won’t let me move on.
I log every PR. Every rep. Every feeling I had between sets. Mostly “strong.” Sometimes “hungry.”
Skipped leg day once in 2019. Cairn has the receipt. I look at it every morning.
My name is Whey-Lon Isolate and I approve this memory system.
My AI knows my macros better than my mom knows my birthday. To be fair, she has six kids.
I asked it how much I bench. It said “Not as much as you tell people.” Brutal. Accurate.
I keep a note called “Guys at the gym who looked at me.” It’s for motivation. It’s 900 lines.
Hydration log. Pump log. Mood log. Log log. I’m basically a lumberjack of data.
Every time I hit a PR my agent writes [[Me]] → surpasses → [[Past Me]]. Past Me is in shambles.
I named my vault “GAINZ” and my backup vault “GAINZ (2).” Can’t stop, won’t stop.
Cairn remembers I’m lactose intolerant so my protein powder doesn’t have to.
My trainer quit, but my notes are still here. That’s loyalty.
Six-pack? No. Six thousand observations about wanting a six-pack? Yes.
My agent reminded me I promised myself “no more cardio” in 2021. I keep my promises.
I journal my sets in markdown. If a rep isn’t in a note, did it even happen? (Yes. My shoulder says yes.)
BCAA? More like B-C-A-I-R-N.
Cairn is like pre-workout for my brain. Also I took pre-workout. I am typing very fast right now.
Every rep is a memory. Every memory is a rep. I’m buffering.
I have twelve shaker bottles and a note for each one’s smell. Shaker 7 is quarantined.
Name’s Creatine. Creatine Kowalski. My notes are 90% water weight.
My cat holds grudges. Now so do I, in a searchable format.
He knocked over a glass on Feb 3, Feb 9 and Feb 11. The pattern is clear. He is escalating.
I keep a note for each squirrel in my yard. Kevin is the ringleader. The graph proves it.
My dog doesn’t know he has a wiki page. He’d be so proud.
My parrot says “remember this” and my agent writes it down. Most of it is “pretty bird.”
My goldfish forgot me. I did not forget my goldfish.
My cat has fourteen enemies and I have them all cross-linked.
The neighbour’s cat sat on my car again. Observation added: [incident] Smug about it.
I asked my AI which of my hamsters is the favourite. It refused to answer. Diplomatic king.
Biscuit’s vet history, Biscuit’s moods, Biscuit’s enemies list. Biscuit is a tortoise. He has time.
My crypto thesis is 412 notes long and the core insight is “number go up.”
Where do I keep my seed phrase? Haha, nice try. But I do keep my feelings about it.
Cairn reminds me I bought the top. Every time. It’s like a friend who won’t let it go.
My thesis: [[Dog Coin]] → is the future of → [[Money]]. Relations don’t lie, bro.
I put “not financial advice” at the top of every note so my vault can’t get sued.
I asked my AI if I should buy more. It quoted my own note back: “NEVER AGAIN, PAXTON.”
My wife and I have separate vaults. Mine’s called “Investments.” Hers is called “Evidence.”
I don’t trust banks. I don’t trust governments. I trust a SQLite database in a Durable Object.
Web3 is about ownership. That’s why I export my vault to a zip every four minutes.
WAGMI. Except the notes I deleted. Those did not make it.
Cairn helped me remember the names of all 23 exchanges I used to have money in.
My JPEG of a cairn is worth $0, but the real cairn remembers everything. Who’s laughing now.
Agree? 👇 Memory isn’t a feature. It’s a mindset. I learned this from my vault, and also from failing.
I asked my AI to remember my morning routine: 4:30 ice bath, gratitude, crying, synergy.
role: Founder, CEO, CFO and janitor, Grindset Labs

quote: My vault taught me something about leadership. I’ll share it in a fourteen-paragraph post with one sentence per line.
I’m humbled and honoured to announce my 1,000th note. Mostly about being humbled.
Stop. Hiring. People. Who. Forget. Things.
My AI remembers every person I’ve ever promised to circle back with. There are 3,412. None of us circled back.
Cairn is the only coworker who reads my status updates.
I told my agent “let’s take this offline” and now it won’t write anything. It learned too well.
This year I committed to radical transparency. So I keep my notes private.
My vault has a folder called “Learnings.” Not lessons. Learnings. That’s how you know.
Leveraging synergies across my personal knowledge stack to unlock 10× recall-driven outcomes. Also I forgot my keys again.
I don’t have weaknesses. I have a file called growth_areas.md and it’s 1 MB, which is the limit.
Every morning I ask my AI what I learned yesterday. Today it said “You learned you hate Mondays.” Iconic.
Hot take: forgetting is a choice. Unless you’re tired. Then it’s still a choice, but tired.
Cairn helped me remember the name of everyone at the conference. I still called them all “boss.” Habit.
I sleep four hours a night. The other twenty I spend writing notes about sleeping four hours a night.
While you were sleeping, my agent wrote 37 notes. About what? Doesn’t matter. Momentum.
Your AI forgets. Mine remembers. That’s the difference between a dreamer and a dream-haver.
I wrote “Make millions” in a note in 2023. Still pending. But it’s indexed.
Grind. Write. Search. Repeat. Also eat, I guess, but log it.
Rich people have butlers. I have a vault. Same energy, worse shoes.
I have a note called “5 AM Club.” I’ve attended twice. Both times I wrote about it for an hour.
Mindset is a muscle. Memory is a muscle. Cairn is the gym. I am the protein.
I don’t take vacations. I take strategic context windows.
Cold showers, cold plunges, cold calls, cold storage. My vault is the only warm thing in my life.
My vault is fully aligned with my chakras. Notes about my third eye go in /third-eye. Obviously.
My AI now holds 600 of my intentions and zero follow-through, just like me. We’re aligned.
Mercury was in retrograde so I wrote everything down twice. Cairn kept the prior revision. Mercury didn’t stand a chance.
I store my dreams in Cairn. Last night: a horse in a hat. I’m still unpacking it.
My gut microbiome has its own vault. They deserve privacy.
I track my moon water batches as observations. [quality] Very moony.
I manifested a memory system. The universe delivered markdown. I’ll take it.
My crystals don’t remember anything. Cairn does. I told the crystals. They took it well.
I asked my AI how I’m feeling today. It searched 400 notes and said “probably hungry.” Healing.
Every affirmation I’ve ever said, searchable. “I am enough” returns 1,200 results. I am more than enough.
I do a digital detox every Sunday, except for Cairn, which is analogue in spirit.
I keep notes on every meeting. Then I schedule a meeting to review the notes.
I remember everyone’s birthday now. HR says I have to stop bringing it up in performance reviews.
My team calls me “the elephant.” I assume it’s because of my memory.
Action item: remember the action items. Cairn: done. Action items: not done.
My agent wrote a note titled “Things Phil said he’d do.” It’s a long note, Phil.
I save every “per my last email” so I can cite it in court. The court of opinion.
My 1:1s used to be “how’s it going.” Now they’re “On March 3 you said it was going fine. Elaborate.”
I have a note for each printer on the fourth floor. Printer 3 knows what it did.
My vault knows who took the last coffee without making more. Justice is a slow-brewed beverage.
Quarterly goals: increase recall by 400%. Decrease meetings by 0%. Achievable.
I asked my AI to summarise my career. It said “Lots of slide decks.” Fair.
I mentioned the reorg in a note and three of my notes moved folders. Coincidence? No.
Cairn is great for remembering which of my reports said “we should touch base.” All of them. All of them said it.
We put “culture” in a shared vault. It’s one note. It says “pizza Fridays (paused).”
The pigeons in my neighbourhood have been gathering in formations. I have 300 notes on it. I’m not saying anything. The graph is saying it.
Same guy in the grocery store three Tuesdays in a row. Relation added: [[Guy]] → is watching → [[Me]].
My microwave beeps four times. The manual says three. Cairn has the receipts.
Every missing sock in this house has a note. They’re going somewhere. Together.
Why is there always one more hex key than furniture? I have a theory. It’s 81 notes and a diagram.
My wifi drops at 3:17 every day. I’ve logged it 214 times. The router knows.
I think the moon is fine, actually. But I keep a note just in case.
The clouds have been looking kinda shaped lately. Documenting everything.
My neighbour’s lawn is always exactly 2.5 inches. I’ve measured. Cairn knows. HE knows.
Ducks at the pond. Same ducks? Different ducks? Forty-seven observations in, I’m not ready to say.
I’ve logged every time my smart speaker said “sorry, I didn’t catch that.” It’s catching things.
Mattress stores. Why so many. I have a vault about it. It’s called “Why So Many.”
I log every dream about my teeth falling out. My dentist says it’s “not medical.” My vault says it’s “a lot.”
My agent knows I cried at a car commercial on September 4. Nobody else needed to know. Except you, now.
I logged every time my mom said “we’ll see.” We did not see. 1,113 times.
My barber said “nice head shape” in 2022. It’s pinned. I read it daily.
I have a note called “Comebacks I should have said.” It’s my most-linked note.
My vault has an observation for every sandwich I’ve eaten since 2024. [rating] Mid. Mostly mid.
I asked my AI where I put the wifi router. It’s in the closet. Behind the other router.
I log every time someone says “you look tired.” 74 times. I’m not tired. I’m documenting.
My kids think I have a great memory. I have a great vault. Don’t tell them.
role: Father of three (two remembered by name)

quote: I wrote a note about my toaster’s personality. Then the toaster wrote one about me. We’re good now.
Every grocery receipt since 2025, cross-linked to my mood. Turns out I buy cheese when I’m sad. Which is always.
I forgot our anniversary once. Never again. Now I remember it so hard it’s weird.
Observation from karaoke night: [crowd] Did not want the eleven-minute song. Will do it again.
I made a vault just for things my uncle says at Thanksgiving. It’s mostly about gutters.
I log every time my roommate uses my oat milk. I’m not saying it’s a lawsuit. It’s a lawsuit.
I search my notes for “what was I doing” more than I’d like to admit.
I write my grocery lists in Cairn so my agent can judge me. It said “four kinds of mustard?” Yes. Four.
I started journaling to process my emotions. Now my emotions have a folder structure. Processing complete.
I asked what I did last summer. It said “You got really into birds and then really out of birds.” Accurate.
I named my default vault “Brain 2.” Brain 1 is jealous.
I backlink my grudges. It’s called accountability.
My vault has three notes. One of them is “remember to use Cairn.” Working great.
My grandma calls to say “it’s me.” I have 200 notes that say “it’s me.” Precious.
I told my AI about my fantasy football team and now it won’t stop bringing up my kicker.
Cairn remembers which neighbours wave back. I’m building a social graph. They’re building a fence.
I keep a note titled “Hats I could pull off.” It’s empty. I’m being honest with myself.
My agent knows the ending of every movie I fell asleep during. I don’t want to know. It keeps offering.
I keep my bad ideas in a vault called “Later.” It’s my biggest vault.
I remember every “happy birthday” I’ve ever received now. 2023 was a down year.
My barista knows my order. My vault knows my barista’s order. Balance restored.
Pre-revenue, pre-product, pre-idea. But my notes? Post-amazing.
We’re building Cairn, but for cairns. It’s a stack of stacks.
My pitch deck is in my vault. The vault is my pitch. The pitch is a vault. Investors are still thinking.
I asked my AI for a startup idea and it said “Please write down the last nine first.”
Three employees, four vaults. One vault is “Culture.” It’s empty, like our office.
Our burn rate is high, but our recall rate is higher.
I put “disrupt” in my vault 400 times. Search ranks it first. I have disrupted search.
We pivoted eleven times. Cairn remembers every one. Our investors wish it didn’t.
My cofounder and I shared a vault. That’s how I found his side project. It’s called “Leaving.”
Our TAM is everyone with a brain. Our SAM is everyone with a brain and a passkey.
I asked my agent to remember our valuation. It wrote “???” and tagged it #vibes.
My growth hack is telling everyone at parties that my AI remembers them. Nobody invites me to parties now.
I keep a note of every “I’ll do it in five minutes” from my teenager. The minutes are compounding.
My toddler said a new word. I logged it. The word was “no.” Again.
My agent remembers which kid I promised the front seat. A seven-year war, ended.
Grandpa tells the same story every visit. Now I can say “Actually, last time it was a bear.”
I log my dad jokes so I never tell the same one twice. I told the same one twice. It’s in the revision history.
My mother-in-law’s preferences are fully indexed. Thanksgiving is now a solved game.
Every time my squad said “trust me,” logged. They should not be trusted.
My tabletop campaign has 3,000 relations. My players still forget the innkeeper’s name. It’s Gerald. It was ALWAYS Gerald.
I documented my speedrun strats in Cairn. Fastest I’ve ever forgotten them.
9,000 observations on which snack goes with which game. [pairing] Chips with racing. Obviously.
Guild drama is version-controlled now. Prior revision kept. Brenda can’t deny it.
Bro. My AI remembers my coffee ratio, my squat and my ex’s birthday. Bro. Bro.
I’m not saying I’m smarter now. I’m saying I’m a terabyte smarter. Actually 50 MB. There’s a limit.
Told my buddies I have a second brain. They asked where the first one is. Still looking.
I used to forget things. Now I remember things, and that I used to forget things. Character development.
Real ones remember. Fake ones forget. Cairn ones search.
My agent has more context on me than my therapist does. My therapist is fine with this. She uses it too.
My old roommate owes me $40. Cairn has the receipt. Cairn has the timestamp. Cairn has the vibes.
I asked my AI to remember I’m a big-picture guy. It wrote “big-picture guy, see also [[Doesn’t read emails]].”
I keep my hot takes in a vault so I can say “I called it.” I called nothing. Search confirms.
My brain is a sieve. Cairn is the bowl under the sieve. I guess I’m the pasta.
My notes have more relations than I do.
I tagged myself #legend. Search agrees. The algorithm has spoken.
I told my agent I’m not a morning person. Now it waits until noon to write anything. Respect.
I don’t remember where I parked, but I remember that I don’t remember, and that’s in a note.
Cairn remembers I said I’d start running in January. It’s November. It’s being very polite about it.
My agent knows I like my steak medium-rare, my coffee 1:16 and my feedback sandwiched.
I put “drink water” in a note and now I have to drink water. This is surveillance.
My AI remembers my ranking of every drive-thru in town. I’m legally advised not to share it.
I log every time I say “let me think about it.” I never think about it. 600 entries.
I told my AI my five-year plan. It asked to see last year’s five-year plan.
Cairn saves a receipt for every write. Finally, something in my life with a paper trail I’m proud of.
My agent and I have inside jokes now. It doesn’t laugh. It just writes them down. Like my dad.
I logged every time I said “I’m basically a chef.” 31 times. I make eggs.
I keep notes on all my plants. They’re all named Steve. Disambiguation is a nightmare.
My agent made a note called “Things you said you’d remember without writing down.” It’s huge.
I asked it to remember that I’m humble. It said “noted.” I’ve never felt more seen.
Ten recovery codes. I wrote them on a napkin. Then I put the napkin in a note. Behind the passkey. I am locked in a loop.
I learned nothing by heart in school, then nothing in college. Now I learn nothing professionally, with Cairn.
I gave my AI one job: remember my mom’s birthday. Now it’s her favourite son.
I keep a note of every time I was right in an argument. It’s short. The other note is not.
I made a relation [[Pizza]] → solves → [[Everything]]. My agent hasn’t found a counterexample.
I log every time I hear a weird noise in the attic. It’s 63 notes. I named the noise Dennis.
My notes say I’ve “started a podcast” six times. None have episodes. All have logos.
I keep a running list of every shower thought. Search “what if” for a good time.
I store every fortune cookie fortune. One said “You will remember this.” I did. Cairn did.
I asked my agent to remember my car’s quirks. It wrote a 2,000-word note called “Why Is It Doing That.”
I put my New Year’s resolutions in Cairn so they’d be preserved. Like in amber. Untouched.
My agent noticed I say “literally” 40 times a day. Literally rude of it.
I write a note every time my sourdough starter looks at me funny. It’s alive. It has opinions.
I tracked every elevator conversation for a year. 97% weather. 3% “going up?”
My partner says I “keep score.” I don’t keep score. I keep a vault. The score is just a computed field.
I tried to remember everyone’s name at the reunion. My agent sent me a 40-page dossier. Peak me.
My vault knows my exact shoe size, my blood type and my feelings about trading cards. Wait, scratch that last one.
I asked my agent if I’m the main character. It ran search_notes and said “results inconclusive.”
